thread.title: Morning Movers: Alibaba Bounces, CBS Climbs, Celgene Gains

author: Barron's
title: Morning Movers: Alibaba Bounces, CBS Climbs, Celgene Gains
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is sinking this morning after the U.S. and China failed to find common ground on trade , and U.S. payrolls disappointed even as the unemployment rate fell to its lowest level since 2000 .
Getty Images S&P 500 futures have fallen 0.5%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have declined 108 points, or 0.5%. Nasdaq Composite futures have dropped 0.6%.
The U.S. economy added 164,000 jobs in April , below the 192,000 that had been predicted by economists, even as the unemployment rate fell to 3.9% for the first time since December 2000. Adding to that disappointment was the lack of progress made by the U.S. and China on trade.
But are earnings the real reason that the major indexes haven't been able to gain traction ?
That's a theory put forward by DataTrek's Nicholas Colas. In a note, he explained that while first quarter earnings have been fantastic-they're growing at a 25.7% clip, according to Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S-second quarter estimates have barely budged. At the end of April, analysts were predicting that earnings will grow by 19.1% during the second quarter, Colas says, up just 0.1 point from the 19% estimate at the beginning of March. And that comes even as sales growth estimates have increased to 8.2% from 7.8%. "At the margin, it implies analysts expect negative earnings leverage versus what they had in their models previously," Colas writes. "When you raise revenue estimates by 10%, for example, earnings should rise by 12% since fixed costs are already baked into the model. When they only go up by 8%, it means costs are rising faster than sales."
And that's a concern that could be around for a while.
Agence France-Presse/Getty Images Alibaba Group Holding ( BABA ) is up 1.8% to $185.67 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The Chinese e-commerce giant earned 91 cents a share on revenue of $9.87 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 88 cents a share on revenue of $9.36 billion. For the full year, it expects revenues to climb 60% to over $63.8 billion, compared with the $54.5 billion consensus.
Apple ( AAPL ) is up 1% to $178.58 after Warren Buffett increased his stake by 45% in the first quarter.
Arista Networks ( ANET ) is down 10% to $241.01 after reporting first-quarter earnings. The cloud networking firm earned $1.79 a share on revenue of $472.5 million, while analysts were looking for earnings of $1.51 a share on revenue of $436.39 million. However, gross margins declined, a trend it expects will continue in the second quarter.
CBS ( CBS ) is up 2.8% to $50.10 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The media firm earned $1.34 a share on revenue of $3.76 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.18 a share on revenue of $3.65 billion. Affiliate and subscription fee revenues were up 16%.
Celgene ( CELG ) is up 1.9% to $87 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The biotech earned $2.05 a share on revenue of $3.54 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.96 a share on revenue of $3.47 billion. For the full year, it expects to earn between $8.70 and $8.90 a share on revenue of $14.8 billion. Analysts are looking for earnings of $8.45 a share on revenue of $14.81 billion.
FMC (FMC) is up 1.2% to $84.70 after Stephens upgraded it to Overweight.
Newell Brands (NWL) is up 3% to $27.50 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The consumer products maker earned 34 cents a share on revenue of $3.02 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 26 cents a share on revenue of $2.95 billion. For the full year, it expects to earn between $2.65 and $2.85 a share on revenue of $14.4 billion to $14.8 billion, while consensus calls for earnings per share of $2.63 on revenue of $14.47 billion. It also agreed to sell the Waddington Group to Novolex for $2.3 billion.
Pandora (P) is up 10.6% to $6.36 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The music streaming service lost 27 cents a share on revenue of $319.2 million, while analysts were looking for a 35 cent per-share loss on revenue of $304.4 million. Total subscribers grew 19% year over year.
Andrew Harrer/Bloomberg Sarepta Therapeutics (SRPT) is down 2.5% to $76.20 after reporting first-quarter earnings .The drug maker lost 28 cents a share on revenue of $64.6 million. Analysts were looking for a 26 cent loss on revenue of $65.3 million. It also announced a partnership with Myonexus Therapeutics to pursue gene therapies for muscular dystrophy.
Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) is down 1.4% to $91 after reporting second-quarter earnings. The chip maker earned $1.64 a share on revenue of $913.4 million, while analysts were looking for earnings of $1.60 a share on revenue of $911.02 million. However, it expects to earn between $1.59 and $1.60 in the third quarter, below the $1.65 per-share consensus estimate.
Twitter ( TWTR ) is down 0.9% to $30.40 as it is urging all users to change their passwords .
World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) is down 1.5% to $40.77 after The Benchmark Company downgraded it to Hold. - Teresa Rivas
